subject: RENEWAL DISCUSSION: RetailCo renewal and expansion proposal
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@retailco.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and capacity bump for FY26Q2

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're kicking off our vendor renewals this week — RetailCo is looking to renew our Redwood contract and increase committed capacity for the coming 12 months. A few specifics from our side:

- Current committed spend covers ~40M tokens/month; we expect peak needs to grow to ~60M tokens/month by July (marketing + search features).
- We need pricing stability through Q3 while we complete our budget approvals.
- Procurement has asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term price hold and an onboarding/expansion credit to offset migration costs.

Can you share options (discounts, credits, or temporary price holds) you can propose? We'd like to present a clean term sheet to procurement by next Monday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Product, RetailCo
[mobile redacted]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@retailco.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity bump for FY26Q2

Hi Sofia — thanks for the note and the context. Congrats on the product ramp — excited to support the growth.

Short answer: we can structure a renewal that includes both a short price hold and a one-time expansion credit, but I want to make sure the numbers and commitment profile align so we balance unit economics and operational capacity.

Could you share a quick usage snapshot (week-of peak and trailing 3 months totals) and confirm whether the 60M tokens/month is a sustained baseline or peak? That will determine the size of the credit and the commit tier we propose.

If you'd like, I can draft a clean term sheet for procurement with two options:
- Option A: 12-month renewal, 3-month price hold at current hosted rates, onboarding credit applied up-front (credit = X% of Q1 invoice) for one-time migration/ops costs.
- Option B: 12-month renewal with a higher committed volume (1.5x current baseline), smaller onboarding credit and a tiered per-token discount after month 3.

I can have the draft to you by Friday if you send the usage data today. If it's helpful, let's schedule 30 minutes to walk procurement through the tradeoffs.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[evelyn_hart@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: renewal-guidance-onepager.pdf (PDF, 28KB)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal and capacity bump for FY26Q2 — ask from RetailCo (context + proposed structure)

Team — forwarding RetailCo's ask. Key points: they want a short price hold while procurement completes approval and an onboarding/expansion credit to help with the migration and initial overage risk. They are likely to commit to higher volume if we can offer an initial stabilization.

My proposed play (to present this week):
- 12-month renewal term starting 2026-04-01.
- Committed capacity: 1.5x current baseline (we'll use their trailing 3-month average to set baseline).
- Price hold: maintain current hosted per-token rate for first 3 months.
- One-time expansion credit: 20% of the first quarter invoice applied as account credit (reduces invoice in month 1-3).
- After month 3: tiered rates based on committed capacity bands (we reduce unit price at tiers to reward higher commit).

Operational ask: we should protect with a 90-day visibility clause (RetailCo provides weekly cadence on forecast) and a hard cap on burst without prior ops approval.

Questions for you:
1) Is 20% one-time credit acceptable from pricing perspective, or should we push to 15%?
2) Can we commit to the 3-month price hold operationally (supporting the burst via our dedicated burst pool if needed)?
3) Any legal flags on the visibility clause wording or the amortization of credits?

Thanks — need quick guidance so I can get a term sheet to procurement by Friday.

—Evelyn

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal and capacity bump for FY26Q2 — ask from RetailCo (context + proposed structure)

Eve — good framing. My quick take:
- Credit: approve but reduce to 15% one-time credit unless they sign a firm 12-month commit at 1.5x baseline. If they want a lower commit, we can keep 20% but shrink price hold to 2 months.
- Price hold: operationally fine for 2–3 months; confirm with ops (Marcus) about burst pool reservation.
- Include SLA language for availability for their production routes to make this higher-value (helps justify concession).

Jordan — can you confirm any wholesale margin constraints for 15% vs 20%? Marcus — confirm capacity reservation turnaround.

Karthik

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@retailco.com>, Procurement <procurement@retailco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RetailCo renewal proposal — staged stabilization and commit-based credit

Hi Sofia (and procurement team),

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Based on your growth profile and our internal alignment, here is a concise proposal we can put in front of procurement this week. This is a single-page summary; I've attached the draft term sheet with redlines and a DocuSign-ready version.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Term: 12 months (2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31).
- Commit: 1.5x trailing 3-month average (we'll finalize baseline after you send the usage CSV).
- Price hold: current hosted per-token rate maintained for months 1–3. No retroactive changes during this stabilization window.
- Expansion credit: one-time credit equal to 20% of estimated Q1 invoices applied as account credit (applied over first invoice cycle; reconciled once we have actual trailing usage).
- Post-stabilization pricing: tiered per-token rates tied to commit bands with an effective unit discount if actual usage reaches the higher commit.
- Operational controls: weekly forecast cadence for the first 90 days; burst above committed band requires ops sign-off to avoid surprise overages.

We expect this structure to (a) give RetailCo procurement the price stability they need for budget sign-off, (b) offset migration/engineering costs via a meaningful up-front credit, and (c) secure Redwood with a meaningful committed volume for the year.

Attachments: Redwood_Renewal_3645_RetailCo_v1.pdf (draft term sheet), usage-summary-q1-2026.csv (we used your sample numbers). DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/s/ABC123-redwood-retailco

If this looks good I'll mark the term sheet as final and route to your Procurement with the DocuSign envelope. If you'd like to tweak credit vs. commit level (e.g., 15% credit for an immediate 2x commit), we can provide a second option in the same doc.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
